summary.intent: Manage the CipherBox v2.0 milestone via /gsd-manager: verify and unblock stuck phases, background-plan and execute phases 74/75/77, ship Phase 74 (WinFsp/FUSE rotation-revocation) and Phase 75 (cross-language IPNS/codec parity) through full CI/review gates, root-cause a macOS-only Desktop-E2E regression, and clean up phase-tracking bookkeeping.
summary.outcome: Phases 69 (false-status bug fixed), 70.1, 74, and 75 were verified/shipped and merged to main; a macOS-only rotation race condition and an access-token TTL bug were root-caused and fixed on PR #607; several hex/base64 and cross-language parity defects were found and fixed on PR #608; phases 76/78/79 remain unplanned per user pause.

repo: GSD's plan-file scanner (plan-scan.cjs:28) has a loose `/PLAN/i` substring fallback that miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' (e.g. '...WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md') as a phase plan, causing false 'partial'/'Executing' dashboard status

GSD's `phase uat-passed --require-verification` predicate downgrades disk_status to 'partial' when implementation is complete and verification passed but no UAT.md file exists, even for phases verified via CI/cargo instead of human UAT
`is_active` in gsd-tools is just 'a file in the phase dir was modified in the last 5 minutes' — not an indicator of a running agent

Sub-agents launched at the repo root cannot EnterWorktree into a pre-existing worktree — the only working pattern for background-continuing worktree-planned phases is sequential main-checkout-on-feat-branch processing

Share API wire fields (encryptedReadKey, encryptedWriteKey, itemNameEncrypted, sharerPublicKey) are validated as HEX by every share DTO on the server, while internal node-codec/sealed-ref fields (readKeySealed, read_sealed) use base64 — identical Uint8Array/key types with opposite encodings and nothing enforcing the right choice at a call site, a recurring source of bugs

commit.gpgsign=false in this repo, so autonomous commits never block on 1Password biometrics; pre-commit hooks are slow (~1-2 min) and can falsely report commit_failed while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1`

macOS desktop-e2e uses FUSE-T with an SMB backend; FUSE-T's overwrite-rename issues an `open()` on the SOURCE file mid-rename, which Linux's kernel rename never does — this is why identical rotation tests pass on Linux/Windows and fail only on macOS

`apply_owned_children` (crates/fuse/src/inode.rs) re-materializes File children with cid=String::new() and a freshly-derived read_key on every metadata refresh, which can clobber a just-rotated inode's correct key if the refresh was in-flight before the rotation completed

`drain_refresh_completions` (crates/fuse/src/fs.rs:~574) already guards against clobbering local mutations via the `mutated_folders`/`publish_queue` sets (uses mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved instead of apply_owned_children), but scope-exit rotations never populated `mutated_folders` because they republish out-of-band via the rotation engine, not the mount publish queue

API access-token TTL is hardcoded 15m (token.service.ts); the desktop-e2e headless test-login binary authenticates once at startup and cannot silently refresh (test-login skips Keychain refresh-token storage), so long-running macOS legs with slow sync waits can 401-lock mid-suite

CBOR duplicate-key rejection: Rust's IPNS record decoder only rejected duplicates of its 4 security-relevant fields (Value/Sequence/Validity/ValidityType), silently ignoring duplicate TTL, while a naive TS `rejectDuplicateMapKeys: true` fix rejects ANY duplicate key — true parity requires both sides to reject any duplicate key

JS regex `$` without the `m` flag matches immediately before a trailing `\n`, so `CANONICAL_UUID_RE.test('...\n')` returns true — a cross-language UUID-validation soundness gap vs Rust's exact byte-length check
cborg (the TS CBOR library) needs an explicit decode option to reject duplicate map keys; Rust's manual CBOR parsing rejects them by default only for specifically-checked fields

code.finding: Fix for the macOS overwrite-rename crash: after refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys, mark rotated folders as mutated_folders so the existing stale-refresh guard in drain_refresh_completions protects them from being clobbered by an in-flight metadata refresh

Grant re-mint's encrypted_read_key must be hex-encoded (not base64) to match the share API wire contract — SC#2 runtime bug (400 Bad Request) that only surfaced in live desktop-e2e, not mocked unit tests
apply_owned_children File arm resets cid to empty string and re-derives read_key on every owned-children materialization, the root cause of the stale-refresh key-clobber bug

rejectDuplicateMapKeys:true in cborg decode call over-corrected vs Rust (which only rejects specific-field duplicates) — Greptile P1 finding fixed by tightening Rust's core/ipns.rs decoders to reject any duplicate key instead

CANONICAL_UUID_RE used JS `$` without `m` flag, accepting a UUID with a trailing newline (37 chars) — Rust rejected it via exact length check; fixed with explicit length guard, real SC3 soundness gap caught by CodeRabbit

workflow: Reproducing a CI-only failure locally (matching exact CI recipe: FUSE-T linking via PKG_CONFIG_PATH override, full 3-layer stack reset of Kubo+DB+journal together) was far faster than iterating via CI dispatch — root-caused a persistent macOS-only bug in ~10 local iterations vs would-be hours of CI round-trips

When a hypothesis is refuted by instrumentation (e.g. API resolve-lag theory disproven by RESOLVE-DEBUG logging), revert the debug instrumentation immediately and pivot rather than patching around a wrong theory

Key-fingerprint instrumentation (logging short hashes of the actual crypto key at each read/write site) was the decisive technique for diagnosing a crypto-key-divergence race that plain error-log analysis and inode-state checks couldn't pin down

GSD's ship-phase flow benefits from running gated audit steps (secure/crypto-review/security-review/simplify) as a background sub-agent in parallel with the separately-run SDK-E2E gate to avoid stack/build contention

CodeRabbit CLI, Greptile, and a dedicated crypto-privacy review agent are complementary — each round of the ship-phase flow caught different real defects on the same PR (CodeRabbit found the UUID soundness gap, Greptile found the reverse dup-TTL divergence from CodeRabbit's own fix), so running all three before merging is worthwhile for crypto-adjacent phases

After a phase auto-closes todos via `resolves_phase` tagging, some todos can be stranded in pending/ despite being genuinely resolved — worth auditing pending todos against the shipped diff+tests when picking up a related phase

Rebasing a background-planned worktree branch onto a newly-merged main can hit STATE.md/ROADMAP.md conflicts from unrelated phase bookkeeping churn; resolving by preferring the phase branch's side is safe since GSD's ship flow regenerates STATE.md anyway

friction: Multiple background planner agents (74, 75, 77) died mid-run from hitting the session quota limit, requiring manual reconstruction of in-flight state from disk (uncommitted plans, worktree branches) rather than trusting agent status notifications

EnterWorktree fundamentally cannot pin a sub-agent launched at repo root into a pre-existing worktree, wasting two agent dispatches before discovering the limitation and pivoting to sequential main-checkout-on-branch processing

Initial rebuild of the desktop binary linked macFUSE instead of FUSE-T (documented gotcha) since the system fuse.pc pointed to macFUSE — required a PKG_CONFIG_PATH override with an aliased fuse.pc to force FUSE-T linkage for accurate macOS reproduction

Author mischaracterized the macOS Desktop-E2E failure as a '401 infra flake' twice before doing rigorous evidence-based diagnosis — user had to explicitly push back with pasted logs to force proper root-causing

Root-causing the macOS overwrite-rename bug took ~10 full local reproduction cycles (~10 min each) across multiple false-start fixes (write_sealed preservation, FilePointer self-heal, coalesced dest-gate) before finding the actual fix — each false start required a full stack reset (Kubo+DB+journal) since partial resets desync
Fixing the macOS overwrite-rename bug incidentally exposed a second latent bug (access-token 15m TTL expiring mid-suite) only once the macOS leg ran long enough to get past the first bug
GitHub CLI `gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL incompatibility, requiring PR body updates via `gh api -X PATCH` instead

Background CI-settle poll for PR 607 sometimes ran against a stale HEAD (before the P1/gap-closure fixes were pushed), requiring manual re-verification of which commit SHA the poll's reported checks actually applied to
